title: When some parts fail, only the failed parts stay ticked
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
  • Inventory parts {Part-A} and {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PARTFAIL-01 and -02) are active at {Location-A}.
  • Their part numbers start with {Prefix-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PARTFAIL).
  • You can open a second browser tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
custom_steps:
1. In browser tab 1, click Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu.
  2. Type {Prefix-A} in the Search box.
  3. Click the ⋮ actions menu button in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  4. Click Deactivate parts.
  5. Click the {Part-A} row.
  6. Click the {Part-B} row.
  7. Open a second browser tab on the same ShopView address and go to Parts → Inventory (tab 2).
  8. In tab 2, type {Part-B} in the Search box.
  9. In tab 2, click the {Part-B} row.
  10. In tab 2, pick Part Status → Inactive.
  11. In tab 2, click Save.
  12. In tab 2, click Deactivate in the "Deactivate part?" confirmation.
  13. Go back to tab 1.
  14. Do not reload tab 1.
  15. In tab 1, click the Deactivate button on the bar.
  16. In tab 1, click Deactivate in the "Deactivate parts?" confirmation.
  17. Wait 15 seconds.
  18. Click Close on the toast.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 12: In tab 2 {Part-B} is deactivated (a "Part deactivated." toast).
  • Step 15: In tab 1 the confirmation reads "2 parts selected."
  • Step 16: A red error toast reads "1 part updated, 1 could not be changed." and lists {Part-B} with the reason "Part is already in that state."
  • Step 16: Bulk mode stays on and only the failed part stays ticked: the bar reads "1 selected" and the {Part-B} row is ticked. {Part-A} has left the Active list.
  • Step 17: The error toast is still on screen after 15 seconds: it stays until closed.
  • Step 18: The toast closes.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk); story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S2-R15, S10-R13, S10-R13a, §8 User Feedback Summary, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 4.3 (Two rows ticked), board 4.4 (Confirm), 13 Oct copy. Story SV-11040 (Verify Phase 3) checklist; Confluence comment 927858689 (Chris Ward, 8 Oct 2026, singular toast). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R15: “When some parts fail, the mode stays on and the selection keeps only the parts that failed.”
  • S10-R13: “For each part that failed, the system names the part by its number and gives the reason.”
  • S10-R13a: “The reasons are "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", "Part not found." and "Part is already in that state."”
  • PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (Bulk change, some parts failed): “"{n} parts updated, {m} could not be changed." ("1 part updated, {m} could not be changed." for one) | Error toast, stays until closed, lists each failed part and its reason”
  • PRD Story 2 context note: “S2-R15 lets the user retry the failures by pressing the button again, instead of finding them by hand.”
  • SV-11040 verification checklist (Verify Phase 3): “Partial failure (one part changed in another tab first) → "1 part updated, 1 could not be changed." listing the reason; only the failed part stays ticked (S2-R15, S10-N2)”
